title: Batching, Queueing & Throughput
interviewAnswer: Batching amortizes fixed overhead and improves accelerator utilization, so throughput rises, but waiting to form batches can increase latency. I choose static, dynamic or continuous batching based on SLA, traffic pattern and model shape.
why: Production capacity is often limited more by poor batching than by raw model speed.
intuition: One GPU prefers doing a useful chunk of work at once; users prefer not waiting for other requests. Serving design balances those goals.
deepDive: For LLMs, sequence lengths vary and continuous batching can admit new requests as others finish. Memory capacity, KV cache and tail latency often determine maximum useful batch size.
workedExample: Batch size 1 may give 40 ms/request at 25 req/s, while batch 16 gives 180 ms/batch ≈89 req/s. Better throughput, worse individual latency.
commonMistakes: Maximizing batch size without considering p95 latency.
Comparing throughput across different input lengths or hardware without normalization.
followUps: How would you design admission control?
production: Autoscaling should consider queue depth, GPU utilization and latency; overload protection is part of correctness.

visual.title: Batch size trade-off
visual.caption: Larger batches often improve throughput while increasing queueing and per-request latency; dynamic batching balances the two.
